text:
deploy-bot: rollout started: service=redwood-inference-api version=v1.4.2 mode=staged target=1% -> scheduled bump to 2% in 5m unless aborted :rocket:

alex: quick note — release notes link: https://internal/docs/releases/v1.4.2 (model routing tweak + kvcache eviction change)

nina: tagging for visibility. ops, watch eu-west and embed latency please.

prashant: on it. I'll keep an eye on 5xx rate and tail latency.

deploy-bot: traffic bumped to 2% at 1751234572 by automated schedule

alex: seeing a small uptick in error rate for eu-west (2xx->5xx) around 1751234578, correlating with long-tail requeue attempts

prashant: can you paste the relevant snippet from logs?

alex: ```
[1751234578] inference-worker-eu-3 ERROR kvcache: failed to restore prefix cache, OOM try=1
[1751234578] inference-worker-eu-3 WARN request: requeueing due to ephemeral failure
```

nina: hmm kvcache eviction change in v1.4.2 could be related. We had a lower memory threshold config enabled for multi-tenant mode.

jamie: ops question — do we want to pin eu-west traffic back to v1.4.1 while we triage, or rollback the canary globally? :thinking_face:

prashant: prefer region pin for now to avoid global churn. We can route eu-west 100% to v1.4.1 and keep the rest of the rollout going.

alex: agreed. how do we pin?

nina: run: `/deploy pin-version --service inference-api --region eu-west --version v1.4.1` (ops role required)

prashant: I'm running the pin now. will confirm when routing flips.

deploy-bot: command accepted: pin-version initiated by prashant at 1751234586. Expected propagation ~30s.

prashant: done — eu-west pinned to v1.4.1. Monitoring metrics now.

alex: 5xx rate in eu-west dropping back toward baseline. tail latency improving.

jamie: good call. Action items: 1) revert kvcache threshold change in v1.4.2 and re-run local membrench; 2) add guard in runtime to avoid aggressive eviction during cold-starts; 3) update release notes with known issue.

nina: I'll open a quick PR for the runtime guard and add an evaluation job against EU traffic samples.

alex: for the staged rollout doc: do we classify this as "regional pin" not a rollback? We should record the decision in the change window notes.

prashant: yes — record as pinned region fallback. No global rollback.

deploy-bot: thread closed for automation: rollout continue rule will resume bumping in other regions. Manual override required to resume eu-west canary.

jamie: filing the post-action note now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
